bluf: Ayima is a UK based enterprise technical SEO consultancy, on record since 2007, with consulting teams under Europe and North America headings and ownership not disclosed. It sells senior led SEO consulting, migrations, competitive SEO, links and an SEO for AI line; its AI posture is Ayima AI, an in-house co-pilot for technical SEO teams. Where it is going is not stated: the record holds no dated move, news, case study, job or pricing signal. A rival should know that all 7 clients on its book are logos with no described work, two of them (SharkNinja, Verizon) shop with other tracked agencies, and its Monsoon read is Onshore wind.

The headline claim, quoted as a claim, is enterprise SEO trusted since 2007 by brands such as Wells Fargo, SharkNinja, QVC and Elsevier; the homepage cites SEO work since 2007 for Verizon, Macy's, QVC and Wells Fargo.

The sold mix is narrow: breadth is 4 lines and only SEO scores 3, with the title and H1 leading on enterprise SEO and the homepage listing consulting, enterprise and competitive SEO and migrations. The service list is SEO Consulting, Enterprise SEO, Competitive SEO, Site Migrations, SEO for AI and Links. AI Automation / Agents, AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR each score 1 with no evidence note; every media, commerce, data, local and web line scores 0. The one proprietary product is Ayima AI, described as an AI co-pilot for technical SEO teams. No partners are listed.

AI posture in plain terms: it promotes Ayima AI as an in-house co-pilot that answers site performance questions for technical SEO teams, and sells an SEO for AI service line; the Horus move read marks P1 partial because no audited AI visibility product (tracking, scorecard, citation share) shows in the record. Pricing signals: none. Recent moves: none dated; news, case studies and jobs are all empty. Conspicuously absent for an enterprise SEO consultancy of its kind: no case study describes any of the named brands, no feed, schema or entity work shows, no CMS or tag stack is recorded for its own site, and the sitemap count is 0, so the record cannot say whether it publishes at all.

Two of the 7 also sit on other tracked agencies' books: SharkNinja appears with brave-bison and peak-ace, and Verizon with publicis-sapient and mod-op. The shared count is 2, both flagged as clients that shop; the whole book, 7 of 7, is names only, which the openings read calls thin evidence.

A rival with a described enterprise migration or technical SEO case is likely to win a hearing at any of the seven by asking what Ayima has done for them lately (moderate confidence: the record does not say which logos are current). Falsifier: case studies naming current work for those brands.

Monsoon reads Onshore wind at 66.4 with an in-house claim attached to Ayima AI: an offshore delivered technical SEO offer can very likely undercut it line by line, and the in-house wording is a claim to test in the sales room.
